land.text: Tbilisi and the neighbouring lands, taken by Marwan II and given to an Arab emir

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Established: 736'; the article text gives 735 for Marwan II's capture of Tbilisi.

land.text: Tbilisi, captured by David IV in February 1122; the emirate's post survived as a governorship of the city

capitals.name: al-Tefelis (Tbilisi)
capitals.note: The emirate was the city and its lands; the infobox gives the capital as al-Tefelis.

rulers.name: Isma'il b. Shuab
rulers.note: Emir list from the article's table; the first emir's reign is given only as 'until 813', so 736 is the emirate's founding year. City councils ruled 1062-1068 and 1080-1122 and are not listed.

correction.text: Tbilisi and the neighbouring lands: 'ruled over the parts of today's eastern Georgia' from its base at Tbilisi

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 736-1122. The article gives no area and no boundary with Kartli, Kakheti, Armenia or Shirvan, so the emirate is drawn as Tbilisi with a 30 km radius (the same reading the Principality of Iberia dossier uses for the 736 loss). Rendering agents should expect a soft city-state; the rest of Kartli is the Georgian kings' or Iberian princes' land.

region.text: Tbilisi and the neighbouring lands, ruled by an Arab emir

ledger.note: 736: the Arabs install an emir at Tbilisi. Infobox 'Established: 736'; 'Marwan II took hold of Tbilisi' in 735 and installed an Arab emir (the article's own 735 and the infobox's 736 differ by a year). The caliph, 'occasionally the ostikan of Armiya', confirmed the emirs.

region.text: central Iberia, which the Arabs had seized after Ashot I's death

ledger.note: 853: Bagrat I of Iberia, backing Bugha al-Kabir's punitive expedition, retakes central Iberia (Kartli) from Arab control. 'In 853, now supporting Bugha al-Kabir, Bagrat regained central Iberia, but only for a brief time.' The Emirate page adds that Bugha burned Tbilisi and had Emir Ishaq executed that year.
854: the Bagratid hold on central Iberia is over. The page says only 'for a brief time' and that the Abkhazians then forced Bagrat out; the year is a bridge (mirrors kingdom-of-the-iberians).

1068: the Seljuks hand the emirate to Fadlun of Ganja. The emirs' table gives 'Fadlun of Ganja 1068-1080', 'appointed by Alp Arslan', after a city council ruled 1062-1068; the Seljuk wars page: 'As the Sultan passed, he gave the small emirate to Fadl ibn Shavur' (Alp Arslan's suzerainty; Bagrat IV received his surrender). The page gives no border change.

region.text: Tbilisi, taken by the Georgians in February 1122

ledger.note: February 1122: David IV captures Tbilisi. 'Once the Seljuks were defeated, the sovereign focused on capturing Tbilisi from the beginning of 1122' and took it 'in February'; the Emirate page: 'In 1122, the king was able to capture Tbilisi', ending 'its approximately 400-year existence'; the Seljuk wars page calls it 'the last Muslim enclave remaining from the Seljuk occupation'.

region.text: Tbilisi, annexed to the Kingdom of Georgia

ledger.note: February 1122: the Emirate of Tbilisi ends and Tbilisi becomes the Georgian capital ('the king transferred the capital from Kutaisi to Tbilisi'); the post of emir was kept 'as governor of the city, until the 18th century'.

wars.name: Bugha al-Kabir's expedition to Tbilisi
wars.outcome: Bugha al-Kabir burned Tbilisi and executed Emir Ishaq; Bagrat I of Iberia, on Bugha's side, held central Iberia only briefly.
wars.note: 'in 853 Caliph al-Mutawakkil dispatched a punitive expedition led by Bugha al-Kabir.' No border change is recorded on the page; the Iberian side is the contest_start/contest_end pair in the ledger.

wars.name: Guaram's seizure of Emir Gabulots
wars.outcome: Guaram 'seized the Bagratids' traditional foe, the Arab emir of Tbilisi, named Gabulots' and sent him to Constantinople; the page credits the episode with winning Guaram Trialeti and Javakheti.
wars.note: The emirs' table in the Emirate article lists Gabuloc 878-880. The page does not say Tbilisi itself changed hands.

wars.name: Georgian capture of Emir Jafar III and siege of Tbilisi
wars.outcome: Georgian nobles 'lured Emir Jafar of Tbilisi from the city and captured him' in 1032; after a two-year siege Bagrat offered a truce to Jafar and the Georgian troops left Tbilisi, a withdrawal the article ties to the Seljuks' entry into Armenia and Azerbaijan.
wars.note: The article gives 1032 only for the capture of Jafar; the siege and truce are undated, so the war is listed at 1032 with no zone.

wars.name: Capture of Tbilisi by David IV
wars.outcome: After Didgori (August 1121) David IV took Tbilisi in February 1122, ending the emirate; the city became the royal capital.
wars.note: Month from the David IV page; the Seljuk wars page dates the capture only to 1122.

certainty.note: No page gives the emirate's frontier; the city and its lands are drawn as a soft radius for the whole life.

sources.title: Emirate of Tbilisi
sources.note: Identity, emirs' table, 853, 1032, 1068, 1122; no area and no boundary.

sources.title: David IV of Georgia
sources.note: February 1122 capture of Tbilisi, capital move, the emir kept as governor.

sources.title: Georgian%E2%80%93Seljuk wars
sources.note: 1068 Fadl ibn Shavur, 1122 'last Muslim enclave'; no Tbilisi siege by Bagrat IV on this page.

notes: Cliopatria has no row for the emirate (its Georgia row begins 724). Page budget 4 pages; none gives an area or a frontier, so the single keyframe is Tbilisi + 30 km, a reading shared with principality-of-iberia (736 loss). Nominal period 1080-1122 (city councils, Seljuk suzerainty) is drawn as the same city. Counterpart notes for other dossiers: (1) kingdom-of-georgia /ledger 1122 gain names great-seljuk-empire; the land was the emirate's (this dossier's loss counterpart is kingdom-of-georgia). (2) The caliph (Umayyad, then Abbasid) confirmed the emirs and the Seljuks held suzerainty from 1068; abbasid-caliphate and great-seljuk-empire may wish a vassal_start for emirate-of-tbilisi. (3) 1032-c.1034 Georgian siege and truce undated on the page. (4) The Emirate page calls Fadlun 'of Ganja' and gives no dynasty. (5) wikidata id null: Wikidata is unreachable and Cliopatria has no row.
